intro: Learn how to talk about hobbies and leisure activities, distinguishing between jugar and tocar.
b1.texto:
Spanish uses two different verbs where English uses *play*:

- For sports and games, use **jugar a** + article: **juego al fútbol**, **al tenis**, **a las cartas** (*a + el = al*).
- For musical instruments, use **tocar** + article: **toco la guitarra**, **el piano**.

The verb **jugar** has a stem change (u → ue) in stressed forms: *juego, juegas, juega, juegan* (but *jugamos, jugáis*).

Other common leisure activities: **hacer deporte**, **ver la tele**, **escuchar música**, **leer**, **nadar**, **pasear**, **ir de compras**, **viajar**.
b2.titulo: What do you do in your free time?
b4.texto: Compare playing an instrument with playing a sport or game.
b6.pregunta: How do you say playing a musical instrument in Spanish?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! Musical instruments always take tocar.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Jugar is used for sports and games, never instruments.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Hacer is not used with instruments.
b7.pregunta: Choose the contracted form to play a sport.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct! Jugar a + el tenis contracts to al tenis.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The mandatory preposition a is missing.
p.escuchar música.consejo: Takes direct object música without prep.
p.jugar al fútbol.consejo: Uses contraction al in standard Spanish.
p.jugar al tenis.consejo: Uses contraction al in standard Spanish.
p.juego.consejo: First person singular with stem change.
b2.f0.texto: What do you do in your free time?
b2.f1.texto: I like reading and playing the guitar.
b2.f2.texto: Do you play football with your friends?
b2.f3.texto: No, I play tennis on Saturdays.
b2.f4.texto: I love swimming and going for walks.
b2.f5.texto: On Sundays I watch TV or travel.
b4.e0.texto: We play the piano and sing songs.
b4.e1.texto: The boys play cards at the club.
b5.f0.texto: Having free time to do sport outdoors is very healthy.
b5.f1.texto: Pablo loves playing football and swimming in the Olympic pool.
b5.f2.texto: In the afternoons I usually go for a walk in the green park with my family.
b5.f3.texto: Lucía prefers playing the piano and listening to relaxing music at home.
b5.f4.texto: At weekends we go out with friends to go shopping in the town centre.
b5.f5.texto: On holiday we love travelling to faraway cities to have a good rest.
p.juegas.consejo: The u becomes ue in «juego», «juegas», «juega»; «jugamos» keeps the u.
p.fútbol.consejo: The stress is on the first syllable and the word ends in l, so it needs an accent: FUT-bol.
p.tenis.consejo: It comes from English but is said TE-nis, with only one n. You play it with «jugar al tenis».
p.tocamos.consejo: Musical instruments go with «tocar», not «jugar»: «tocamos el piano».
p.cantamos.consejo: The «nosotros» form of «cantar»; it is in the same family as «la canción» (song).
p.canciones.consejo: Plural of «canción»: the accent disappears, and the c before i sounds like th.
p.chicos.consejo: The «ch» sounds like in «chocolate». The feminine is «chicas»; «los chicos» can also mean boys and girls.
p.club.consejo: It comes from English and has one syllable: klub. The plural is «clubes».
p.olímpica.consejo: The stress falls on the third syllable from the end, so it has an accent: o-LIM-pi-ka. Masculine: «olímpico».
p.fascina.consejo: Works like «gustar»: «nos fascina viajar». The «sc» sounds like s + th: fas-THI-na.
p.ciudades.consejo: Singular: «la ciudad». The d is soft, never th: thyu-DA-des.
p.lejanas.consejo: It comes from «lejos» (far). The j sounds like a strong h: le-HA-nas.
p.toco.consejo: «Tocar» also means to touch. With an instrument it means to play it: «toco la guitarra».
p.guitarra.consejo: The «gui» sounds like «gi», with a silent u, and the rr is rolled: gi-TA-rra.
